name: Java Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) Engine
short_description: A Java-based Deep Packet Inspection engine that captures live network traffic, analyzes packets across multiple protocol layers, classifies traffic, manages network flows, detects suspicious activities, calculates traffic statistics, identifies top talkers, and generates CSV, HTML dashboard, and PDF reports.
problem_statement: Traditional network monitoring tools may provide traffic statistics without giving a clear view of individual packets, protocols, flows, and suspicious activities. This project aims to build a modular Java-based DPI engine that can inspect live network traffic, extract useful packet-level information, identify network behavior, detect potential port scans, and present the collected information through structured reports and a dashboard.
objective: To develop a practical network traffic analysis and security monitoring application using Java that captures live packets, parses network protocols, tracks flows, detects suspicious scanning behavior, calculates traffic statistics, identifies top communicating hosts, and generates human-readable reports.

dataset.name: Live Network Traffic
dataset.size: Varies depending on the packet capture session
dataset.source: Captured from the local network interface using Pcap4J
dataset.details: The project does not rely on a fixed machine-learning dataset. It processes live network packets captured from a selected network interface. During testing, the engine analyzed traffic containing IPv4, TCP, UDP, HTTP, HTTPS, LLMNR, NetBIOS and other network traffic.

features.name: Live Packet Capture
features.purpose: Captures network packets from a selected network interface using Pcap4J.

features.name: Ethernet Parsing
features.purpose: Analyzes Ethernet frames and identifies the Ethernet type, such as IPv4, IPv6 or ARP.

features.name: IPv4 Parsing
features.purpose: Extracts IPv4 source and destination addresses and analyzes IPv4 traffic.

features.name: TCP Parsing
features.purpose: Extracts TCP source port, destination port and TCP-related information from packets.

features.name: UDP Parsing
features.purpose: Analyzes UDP packets and extracts source and destination port information.

features.name: TCP Flag Analysis
features.purpose: Analyzes TCP flags such as SYN, FIN, ACK, PSH and other combinations for traffic classification and security detection.

features.name: HTTP Parsing
features.purpose: Identifies HTTP requests and extracts information such as method, path, HTTP version, host and user-agent when the payload is available.

features.name: DNS Parsing
features.purpose: Provides DNS protocol analysis and supports identification of DNS-related traffic.

features.name: Traffic Classification
features.purpose: Classifies captured traffic into application or service categories such as HTTP, HTTPS, DNS, LLMNR and NetBIOS.

features.name: Flow Management
features.purpose: Groups packets into network flows using communication endpoints and tracks packet count, bytes, first-seen time and last-seen time.

features.name: Port Scan Detection
features.purpose: Detects potentially suspicious scanning behavior based on TCP flag patterns and connection activity.

features.name: Top Talker Detection
features.purpose: Identifies hosts responsible for the highest amount of observed network traffic.

features.name: Traffic Statistics
features.purpose: Calculates total packets, bytes, TCP flows, UDP flows and application-level traffic statistics.

features.name: CSV Reporting
features.purpose: Exports flow-level information such as source IP, destination IP, ports, protocol, service, packets, bytes and duration.

features.name: HTML Dashboard
features.purpose: Provides an interactive dashboard containing threat statistics, flow summaries, charts and a searchable flow table.

features.name: PDF Reporting
features.purpose: Generates a structured PDF report containing report timestamp, traffic summary, threat summary and flow details.

best_result.metric: Successful live traffic analysis and reporting
best_result.value: Successfully captured and analyzed live packets and generated CSV, HTML and PDF reports
best_result.model: Not applicable - this is a rule-based network security and packet analysis project

challenges: Understanding raw network packet structure and protocol layers
Capturing live packets correctly from the network interface
Parsing different packet types such as Ethernet, IPv4, TCP and UDP
Designing a reliable network flow representation
Keeping dashboard, CSV and PDF statistics consistent
Generating a professional PDF report from collected network statistics
Debugging Maven and Java dependency issues
Managing generated reports without accidentally committing temporary build files to GitHub
solutions: Used Pcap4J to handle low-level packet capture and packet structures instead of manually processing raw bytes
Separated packet processing into modular parser classes for Ethernet, IPv4, TCP, UDP, HTTP and DNS
Created Flow and FlowManager components to maintain and aggregate communication flows
Created dedicated statistics classes to calculate packet, byte, protocol and host-level statistics
Implemented TCP flag analysis to identify patterns associated with SYN, FIN, NULL and XMAS scans
Created HostStatisticsManager to calculate traffic contribution and identify the top talker
Used a centralized ReportGenerator to generate CSV and HTML reports from the collected flow information
Used OpenPDF through a dedicated PDFReportGenerator for structured PDF reports
Used Maven to manage project dependencies and build the Java application
Used Git and GitHub to version-control the source code while excluding generated build files and temporary files through .gitignore

my_contribution: I designed and developed the Java Deep Packet Inspection project as a hands-on learning project. I worked on the packet capture workflow, protocol parsing, traffic classification, flow management, statistics collection, security detection, top-talker analysis and CSV/HTML/PDF report generation. I also handled Maven configuration, debugging, project organization, Git/GitHub version control and testing with live network traffic. During development, I used ChatGPT as a learning and debugging assistant to understand networking and Java concepts, troubleshoot implementation issues, and improve the project structure. I then implemented, tested and verified the functionality myself.
